text:
mike_support: FYI customer ACME is failing to complete OAuth with both GitHub and Google — getting a state mismatch on the callback :thinking:
jamie_se: Can you paste the exact callback URL they land on and any error from our logs? Also which proxy/load balancer in front of their app?
mike_support: Customer pasted this error page: \n\n  ERROR: OAuth callback failed (400) - invalid_state
  expected state: "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1...long...NzI"
  got state: "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1...long...Nz"

Looks like the trailing chars are cut off. They mention CloudFront + our ALB + an internal proxy.
ev an_repro: reprod note: this smells like cookie/header truncation or URL length trimming by an intermediate proxy. common culprits: cookie chunking, path rewriting, or char limit on query param via edge. ask them to capture the full redirect from the browser network tab (preserve headers). also check if they use any iframe/deeplink.
mike_support: customer sent the redirect URL (URL-encoded):\n\n  https://app.acme.example/oauth/callback?code=02b...&state=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJ1c2VyIjoic...%E2%80%A6

you can see the URL ends with %E2%80%A6 which is the UTF8 ellipsis — the client/browser truncated/ellipsized it when copying. but server logs show truncated value without expected suffix.
jamie_se: Can we confirm whether our SDK/state generator ever contains characters that some proxies might escape (e.g., plus signs, percent encoding, emoji)? We recently added emoji to org names for debug tokens.
ev an_repro: Good catch — plus signs and percent encodings are fragile. We should check two things: 1) whether the state is being stored as a cookie and exceeds the cookie chunk size, 2) whether any intermediate component rewrites or normalizes query strings. Ask ACME to run this curl to reproduce and return the raw Location header: \n\n  curl -i -s -L -o /dev/null -w '%{redirect_url}\n' -D - "https://auth.redwood.ai/authorize?client_id=acme&redirect_uri=https://app.acme.example/oauth/callback&response_type=code&state=TEST_STATE_WITH_SPECIAL_CHARS%2B%25%F0%9F%98%81"

This will show how the redirect is emitted by our auth endpoint vs what the browser follows.
sarah_research: Another potential is SameSite=None cookie being dropped in some webviews or iOS WKWebView. If the state is stored only in a cookie (vs server side session) the callback may not match. Recommend we ask ACME to try in an incognito Chrome desktop to narrow webview vs network proxy.

mike_support: Sent repro instructions and requested raw headers. Ticket created: #INC-2024-873 (support-bot attached). They replied with the header dump: \n\n  Location: https://app.acme.example/oauth/callback?code=02b...&state=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJ1c2VyIjoiYWNtZS1zZXNzaW9uIiwiYWNjIjoxMjN9.TRUNCATED
  Set-Cookie: rwd_state=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...; Path=/; Secure; SameSite=None; HttpOnly

Looks like our Location has full state but downstream show TRUNCATED in network capture.
jamie_se: If our Location is correct but the browser gets truncated, the problem is between our redirect and the client's browser — likely a proxy or CDN rewriting/limiting URL length or sanitizing '%'. Ask for upstream proxy config (max header size, uri length). Also check whether their client-side load balancer does percent-decoding early and then re-encodes incorrectly.
ev an_repro: Quick mitigation we can offer: enable server-side state persistence for that org (store code_verifier/state server-side keyed by a short opaque id in the redirect URL). Then state in query is only a short id (<32 chars) and avoids long token fragmentation. I can draft a minimal patch/guide.
mike_support: I told them workaround and we opened a dedicated posture: engineer evan_repro will help with config changes. Also asked them to whitelist our redirect host path through their CF worker (if they use one) and to lift any 2048 char URL limits temporarily.
support-bot: Ticket INC-2024-873 linked to support Jira: RDW-4219. Assigned to evan_repro.

jamie_se: Follow-ups: collect their proxy type/version, CloudFront behavior (if any Lambda@Edge), and full raw Location header from the first redirect (not ellipsized by browser devtools). If they can't capture it, ask them to curl our /authorize with the same client_id and check headers. We'll coordinate a joint repro session if needed. :+1:

mike_support: Thanks — leaving notes in ticket, will update when ACME shares proxy config and raw headers.
